metadata.title: A Plan, Not a Guess.
metadata.subtitle: The Claude Margin Analyzer Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to check your margins, is it improvising a method, or following a written plan? Lands the carry-out that margin-analyzer is a written plan Claude follows -- the same steps every run -- and it only ever covers what that plan says.

beats.narration_text: Someone wonders whether Claude just invents a plan for checking margins. It doesn't — it follows one, a written skill called margin-analyzer. Let's open it up.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is margin-analyzer — built, going by its name, for a small business checking its profit margins. The SKILL.md file holds the whole instruction set in plain language, no hidden code. Claude reads the file, then acts on exactly what it says.
The instructions live in a Steps section, numbered in order. Claude reads step one, does it, then moves to step two — straight through, no branching unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: STEPS, IN ORDER
production_viz.caption: no branching unless a step says so.

beats.narration_text: Here's the part worth knowing: margin-analyzer is a plan, not a guess. Every run, Claude checks the numbers the same way, in the same order — that's what makes the result repeatable. It's also the limit: anything the plan doesn't cover, the skill doesn't do.

production_viz.label: REPEATABLE — AND LIMITED
production_viz.caption: the plan is also the boundary.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a written plan Claude follows, not a fresh guess it invents each run — the same steps, every time, and nothing beyond what the plan says.

props.quote: A Skill is a written plan Claude follows, not a fresh guess it invents each run — the same steps, every time, and nothing beyond what the plan says.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want a repeatable way to check profit margins across a list of products, using the cost and price for each one. Write me a short, numbered set of steps — like a Skill file — that says exactly what to check, in what order, so running it twice on the same numbers gives the same answer. Then tell me one thing that plan wouldn't catch.
